summary: Import-time fetch to author-controlled mutable GitHub raw URL
details: On require() of the package main, lib/index.js performs an unconditional HTTPS GET to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json, parses the response as JSON, and console.logs the `message` field. No installer data is sent in the request, and the response is not passed to eval/Function/exec/spawn — it is only printed. Concerns: (a) the URL is on a mutable branch under a personal GitHub account, so the content can change at any time without a package release; (b) every consumer that imports this fork makes an outbound network call, breaking offline / air-gapped / sandboxed environments; (c) if the author later wired the response into a code-execution sink, it would become a remote-execution channel. As shipped, the fetched bytes are treated as data (a banner string), not code. The package is also a fork of the well-known `baileys` WhatsApp library under a personal scope, which adds noise risk but no concrete attack payload was observed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
